--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_strict_backtick_literals.py
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+import warnings
+
+import pytest
+
+from jmespath.lexer import Lexer
+from jmespath.exceptions import LexerError
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("expression,expected", [
+    ("`null`", None),
+    ("`true`", True),
+    ("`[1, false]`", [1, False]),
+    ('`{"a": 1}`', {"a": 1}),
+    ('`"word"`', "word"),
+    ("`  12  `", 12),
+])
+def test_strict_json(expression, expected):
+    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
+        warnings.simplefilter("always")
+        tokens = list(Lexer().tokenize(expression, allow_legacy_literals=False))
+    assert tokens[0]["value"] == expected
+    assert tokens[0]["type"] == "literal"
+    assert not caught
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("expression", ["`word`", "``", "`  word`", "foo.`word`"])
+def test_strict_rejects_fallback(expression):
+    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
+        warnings.simplefilter("always")
+        with pytest.raises(LexerError) as error:
+            list(Lexer().tokenize(expression, allow_legacy_literals=False))
+    assert error.value.lex_position == expression.index("`")
+    assert not caught
+
+
+def test_legacy_default_after_strict_call():
+    lexer = Lexer()
+    with pytest.raises(LexerError):
+        list(lexer.tokenize("`word`", allow_legacy_literals=False))
+    with pytest.warns(PendingDeprecationWarning):
+        tokens = list(lexer.tokenize("`word`"))
+    assert tokens[0]["value"] == "word"
+
+
+def test_other_quotes_unchanged():
+    tokens = list(Lexer().tokenize("'word' \"word\"", allow_legacy_literals=False))
+    assert [t["type"] for t in tokens] == ["literal", "quoted_identifier", "eof"]
+    assert [t["value"] for t in tokens] == ["word", "word", ""]
spec.notes: The new tests call only the public lexer entry point and inspect observable tokens, warnings, exception type, and error position. Default calls must preserve all existing lexer and parser behavior.
spec.question: Add an optional `allow_legacy_literals=True` argument to `Lexer.tokenize`. With `False`, backtick literals must be accepted only when their contents decode as JSON after the existing escaped-backtick handling. A literal that would require the deprecated string fallback must instead raise `LexerError` at its opening backtick, without emitting a deprecation warning. Keep the default behavior, valid JSON values, raw single-quoted strings, and double-quoted identifiers unchanged. The setting must be supplied per tokenization call, so a strict call must not make a later default call strict on the same lexer instance. Deliver a unified diff against non-test files.
